source_text: Οὐ γὰρ μωραίνομεν, ἄνδρες Ἕλληνες, οὐδὲ λήρους ἀπαγγέλλομεν, θεὸν ἐν ἀνθρώπου μορφῇ γεγονέναι καταγγέλλοντες. Οἱ λοιδοροῦντες ἡμᾶς συγκρίνατε τοὺς μύθους ὑμῶν τοῖς ἡμετέροις διηγήμασι. Δηΐφοβος, ὥς φασιν, ἦν ἡ Ἀθηνᾶ διὰ τὸν Ἕκτορα, καὶ χάριν Ἀδμήτου Φοῖβος ἀκειρεκόμης τὰς εἰλίποδας βοῦς ἐποίμαινε, καὶ πρεσβύτις ἀφικνεῖται πρὸς τὴν Σεμέλην ἡ τοῦ Διὸς γαμετή.Τοιαῦτα δὲ μελετῶντες πῶς ἡμᾶς διαγελᾶτε; Τέθνηκεν ὑμῶν ὁ Ἀσκληπιός, καὶ ὁ τὰς πεντήκοντα παρθένους μιᾷ νυκτὶ Θεσπιάσι διακορεύσας βορᾷ πυρὸς ἑαυτὸν παραδοὺς οἴχεται. Προμηθεὺς τῷ Καυκάσῳ προσαρτηθεὶς τιμωρίαν χάριν τῆς εἰς ἀνθρώπους εὐεργεσίας ὑπήνεγκεν. Φθονερὸς ὁ Ζεὺς καθ᾿ ὑμᾶς, καὶ κρύπτει τὸν ὄνειρον τοῖς ἀνθρώποις βουλόμενος ἀπόλλυσθαι. Διόπερ ἀποβλέψαντες πρὸς τὰ οἰκεῖα ἀπομνημονεύματα κἄν ὡς ὁμοίως μυθολογοῦντας ἀποδέξασθε. Καὶ ἡμεῖς μὲν οὐκ ἀφραίνομεν, φλήναφα δὲ τὰ ὑμέτερα. Γένεσιν ἄν λέγητε θεῶν, καὶ θνητοὺς αὐτοὺς ἀποφανεῖσθε. Διὰ τί γὰρ οὐ κύει νῦν ἡ Ἥρα; Πότερον γεγήρακεν, ἤ τοῦ μηνύσαντος ὑμῖν ἀπορεῖται; Πείσθητέ μοι νῦν, ὦ ἄνδρες Ἕλληνες, μηδὲ τοὺς μύθους μηδὲ τοὺς θεοὺς ὑμῶν ἀλληγορήσητε. Κἄν γὰρ τοῦτο πράττειν ἐπιχειρήσητε, θεότης ἡ καθ᾿ ὑμᾶς ἀνῄρηται καὶ ὑφ᾿ ὑμῶν· οἱ γὰρ τοιοῦτοι παρ᾿ ὑμῖν ὄντες οἱ δαίμονες, ὁποῖοι καὶ λέγονται, φαῦλοι τὸν τρόπον εἰσίν, ἢ μεταγενόμενοι πρὸς τὸ φυσικώτερον οὔκ εἰσιν οἷοι καὶ λέγονται. Σέβειν δὲ τῶν στοιχείων τὴν ὑπόστασιν οὔτ᾿ ἂν πεισθείην, οὔτ᾿ ἂν πείσαιμι τὸν πλησίον.Καὶ Μητρόδωρος δὲ ὁ Λαμψακηνὸς ἐν τῷ περὶ Ὁμήρου λίαν εὐήθως διείλεκται, πάντα εἰς ἀλληγορίαν μετάγων. Οὔτε γὰρ Ἥραν οὔτε Ἀθηνᾶν οὔτε Δία τοῦτ᾿ εἶναί φησιν ὅπερ οἱ τοὺς περιβόλους αὐτοῖς καὶ τεμένη καθιδρύσαντες νομίζουσι, φύσεως δὲ ὑποστάσεις καὶ στοιχείων διακοσμήσεις. Καὶ τὸν Ἕκτορα δὲ καὶ τὸν Ἀχιλλέα δηλαδὴ καὶ τὸν Ἀγαμέμνονα καὶ πάντας ἁπαξαπλῶς Ἕλληνάς τε καὶ βαρβάρους σὺν τῇ Ἑλένῃ καὶ τῷ Πάριδι, τῆς αὐτῆς φύσεως ὑπάρχοντας, χάριν οἰκονομίας ἐρεῖτε παρεισῆχθαι, οὐδενὸς ὄντος τῶν προειρημένων ἀνθρώπων. Ταῦτα δὲ ἡμεῖς προετείναμεν ὥσπερ ἐπὶ ὑποθέσεως· τὴν γὰρ ἡμετέραν περὶ τοῦ θεοῦ κατάληψιν οὐδὲ συγκρίνειν ὅσιον τοῖς εἰς ὕλην καὶ βόρβορον κυλινδουμένοις.
pass_a_gloss: For we do not speak foolishly, men of Greece, nor do we announce empty words, proclaiming God to have come in human form. You who revile us, compare your myths to our stories. Deiphobus, as they say, was loved by Athena on account of Hector, and Phoebus, unshorn, herded the curl-horned oxen for the sake of Admetus, and an old woman came to Semele, the bride of Zeus. Studying such things, how do you laugh at us? Your Asclepius died, and the one who corrupted the fifty virgins of the Thespians in one night, having been consumed by fire, departed. Prometheus, having been bound to the Caucasus, endured punishment for the benefit he conferred on humans. Zeus is envious towards you, and hides dreams from humans, wishing them to perish. Therefore, looking at your own memories, even if you consider us to be mythologizing in a similar way, accept us. We do not speak foolishly, but we despise your things. You might tell the birth of the gods, and you will declare them to be mortal. Why does Hera not conceive now? Has she grown old, or is she at a loss because the one who announced it to you is absent? Be persuaded by me now, men of Greece, and do not allegorize your myths or your gods. For even if you try to do this, the divinity according to you is destroyed and by you; for the such-like beings among you, who are called demons, are of a base character, or having come later, they are not as they are said to be, according to what is more natural. I would not be persuaded to reverence the substance of the elements, nor would I persuade the one next to me. Metrodorus of Lampsacus also, in his work on Homer, has spoken very piously, transferring everything to allegory. He says that neither Hera nor Athena nor Zeus is what those who have built temples and precincts around them think, but rather they are substances of nature and adornments of the elements. And he would say that Hector and Achilles and Agamemnon and all the Greeks and barbarians, along with Helen and Paris, being of the same nature, were introduced for the sake of economy, none of the aforementioned people being real. We have proposed these things as if on a hypothesis; for it is not holy to compare our conception of God to those who are rolled in matter and mud.

choices.english: God to have come in human form

pass_b_english: We do not speak foolishly, men of Greece, nor do we proclaim empty words when we announce that God has come in human form. You who revile us, compare your myths to our accounts. They say Deiphobus was loved by Athena because of Hector; Phoebus, unshorn, herded the curl-horned oxen for Admetus' sake; an old woman came to Semele, Zeus's bride. Pondering such stories, how can you laugh at us? Your Asclepius died; the man who corrupted the fifty Thespian virgins in a single night gave himself to the fire and departed. Prometheus, bound to the Caucasus, suffered punishment for benefiting humanity. Zeus envies you and withholds dreams from humans, wishing them to perish. Therefore, examine your own traditions; even if you deem us to be mythologizing in the same way, accept our message. We are not foolish; we despise your fabrications. You recount the birth of the gods and thereby declare them mortal. Why does Hera not conceive now? Has she grown old, or is she at a loss because the one who announced it to you is absent? Be persuaded, men of Greece: do not allegorize your myths or your gods. Even if you attempt it, the divinity according to you is destroyed by your own hands; for the beings called demons among you are base in character, or, having come later, they are not what they are said to be according to nature. I would not be persuaded to worship the substance of the elements, nor would I persuade my neighbor. Metrodorus of Lampsacus, in his work on Homer, has spoken with excessive piety, turning everything into allegory. He claims that neither Hera nor Athena nor Zeus is what those who built temples and precincts for them believe; rather, they are substances of nature and adornments of the elements. He would say that Hector, Achilles, Agamemnon, all Greeks and barbarians, along with Helen and Paris, being of the same nature, were introduced for the sake of economy, none of those people having actually existed. We have proposed these things as a hypothesis; for it is not holy to compare our conception of God to those who are rolled in matter and mud.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the nuances of the Greek text, including the complex conditional and causal structures regarding the nature of the gods and the critique of allegory. Pass A and Pass B are consistent with the source.

The Greek text is accurately translated in both Pass A and Pass B, with no omissions, additions, or distortions. The citations to Greek myths and figures are correctly represented, and the theological arguments are preserved. The title 'Defense Against Greek Mythology' appropriately reflects the content of the text. No uncertainties or errors are detected in the translation or its alignment with the source.
